entries.note: PMID 16707786 resolves to Wilcock 2006; quote verbatim in abstract. 2H6 as ponezumab's murine parent accepted (product_in_model false).

PMID 29067345 (PET-PIB study); quote verbatim. NCT00945672 confirmed as this study: 36 enrolled, 10 and 7.5 mg/kg arms, Swedish sites; results posted 2024-04-19. Plaque unchanged vs mouse fall: contra holds.

Swanson 2021 quote verbatim; PharmR AD-TR-007 and Lord 2009 abstract both say insoluble Abeta and plaque unchanged in plaque-bearing mice. Contra is defensible, but the model's main readout, protofibrils, was never measured in patients (see rule question).
PMID 22787053 Adolfsson 2012; quote verbatim. No human exposure target stated in the abstract.

Cummings 2018 (PMID 29695589) quote verbatim. 2014 date matches AC Immune release of 16 Jul 2014 (ABBY missed co-primaries); CREAD futility and registry date 2020-07-16 confirmed. Scoring dose with no model-stated target is a rule question.
Quote verbatim in Wilcock 2006 abstract.

ABBY primaries ADAS-Cog12 and CDR-SB confirmed in the abstract and on NCT01343966, with no posted results. Ponezumab NCT00722046 primary is safety (registry), so it rightly stays in patient_trials. Registry date 2022-11-07 confirmed.

The class relied on mAb158's protofibril lowering, not behaviour. Lord 2009: place learning 'depended neither on treatment nor transgenicity', so the test had no deficit to rescue. A null from that test is not a no-benefit prediction. Cell stays contra from entry 2.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 8 and rule 4 (#73): lecanemab advanced on tg-ArcSwe protofibril lowering; the filed fear-conditioning null (W-20100159) and Lord 2009 maze, with no transgenic deficit, were not relied on as a prediction. A non-relied-on insensitive test is untested.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in Wilcock 2006 abstract.

Quote verbatim. The phase 1 claim gives no numbers (data-not-shown style), so confidence should be low, not medium. The microglia assays are in vitro, not ex_vivo patient cells. ABBY's 1 ARIA-E case in 431 supports 'same'.

Landen 2017a quote verbatim; registry date confirmed. The judgement wrongly says no microhemorrhage model was run for lecanemab: PharmR/SumR show mAb158 studies in Tg2576 and APPArcSwe were run despite the 2014 waiver (see missing).
Madrasi 2021 (PMID 33938131, PMC8478725 full text) quote verbatim. Opening untested entry at 2021 first use; class level, crenezumab in model. Model calibrated post hoc to published PET data.

Quote verbatim in PMC8478725. Paper: model calibrated to 'observed PD including Aβ plaque changes measured by PET'; only aducanumab 1-3 mg/kg was 'a priori'. BLAZE PET (Cummings/Salloway 2018, PMC6146627) preceded it, so retro is correct.
Söderberg 2022 (PMID 36253511, PMC10119362) quote verbatim in abstract and full text. Epub 17 Oct 2022. Opening untested entry; ex_vivo for a cell-free binding assay accepted.

Quote verbatim in PMC10119362 full text. Epub 17 Oct 2022, after Study 201 (2018/2021) and Clarity AD topline (27 Sep 2022): retro, not same. Hedged 'may explain' and comparators are non-members; low confidence fits.
Söderberg 2024 (PMID 38740836) quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested entry at 2024 first use; every ARIA-E rate compared was already published.
Quote verbatim in abstract; crenezumab 'negligible CAA fibril binding' with no ARIA-E also stated. All ARIA-E rates (Clarity AD 12.6%, 2022) predate it: retro correct.

PharmR p.27 quote verbatim. W-20090278 and W-20100295 are short-term protofibril studies, not the microhemorrhage studies, but they do date first Tg2576-mAb158 use to ~2009; model_filed wording should say so. Untested holds.

Label (Jan 2023) ARIA-H 6% vs 5% verbatim; PharmR/SumR: no mAb158 microhemorrhage in Tg2576 (4 months, to 50 mg/kg/week). Same holds, assuming the mouse study preceded Study 201 readout; its run date is not stated in the review, only its 2023 publication.

Jul 2023 label (s001) quote verbatim: ARIA-H 17% (152/898) vs 9% (80/897); label adds no increase in isolated ARIA-H. Mouse null from SumR line 347. Contra at medium confidence holds; excess riding with ARIA-E is a caveat, not a reversal.

missing: safety, lecanemab, contra (model_id tg-arcswe-mab158, plus Tg2576 with mAb158), year 2023. FDA SumR, BLA 761269 (sources/761269/761269Orig1s000SumR.txt, line 346): 'In studies specifically conducted with mAb158 to microhemorrhage in Tg2576 and APPArcSwe transgenic mice, no mAb158-related microhemorrhage was seen.' PharmR studies AD-TR-009 (3 months) and the 4-month Tg2576 study are consistent. Patients: Clarity AD (van Dyck 2022, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2212948) had ARIA-E 12.6% (abstract) and excess ARIA-H in the full text; Study 201 had ARIA-E 10% vs 1% in the Jan 2023 label (ARIA-H 6% vs 5%, no excess). The model-side numbers were first public in the Jan 2023 FDA review. Under rule 6 this contra likely sets the safety cell's latest status.

efficacy, lecanemab (only if the protofibril model is scored as predicting benefit): Study 201 missed its 12-month Bayesian ADCOMS primary (64% vs the 80% bar; Eisai release Dec 2017; Swanson 2021, doi 10.1186/s13195-021-00813-8), before Clarity AD met its primary in 2022.
rule_questions: Engagement: when the model's main PD readout (brain protofibrils) was never measured in patients, may the cell be scored on a secondary readout that the model said would NOT move (plaque), where the patient readout moved more than the model predicted? Or is it untested?

Dose: when no member's model stated a human exposure target, does 'reached, failed, abandoned' still give dose contra derived_from efficacy, or is dose untested because there was no target to compare?

Safety and best model: rule 6 makes one drug's contra override another's same within one model. Ponezumab's Tg2576/2H6 model matched (2017) and lecanemab's mAb158 model missed ARIA (2023). These are different models of one class, so which status does the cell show after 2023?

Safety: ARIA-E (edema) cannot be seen with histology in mice. Does a mouse study that reported only microhemorrhage count as silent on ARIA-E (not a miss), leaving only excess ARIA-H in Clarity AD to score?

Efficacy: Study 201 favoured drug in direction (64% probability of a 25% effect) but missed its Bayesian gate. Against a model predicting benefit, is that a primary-endpoint miss (contra) or a directional match?
